t: A series LCR circuit is on 200 V, 50 Hz. If the voltage across the inductor (L = 10 mH) is 31.4 V, the current is
An LCR circuit is at resonance. If R is halved, the current amplitude at resonance will be
s:
At resonance, inductive reactance equals capacitive reactance (X_L = X_C), so the impedance of the circuit is purely resistive:
Z = R

The current amplitude at resonance is given by:
I₀ = V₀ / Z = V₀ / R

This shows that I₀ is inversely proportional to R (I₀ ∝ 1/R).

When the resistance R is halved (R' = R/2):
I₀' = V₀ / (R/2) = 2(V₀ / R) = 2I₀

Thus, the current amplitude is doubled.

Options (A), (C), and (D) are incorrect because the current at resonance is inversely proportional to resistance, so reducing R must increase the current, ruling out zero, remaining unchanged, or being halved.

Correct Answer: (B) double

t: A capacitor has capacity C and reactance X. If capacitance and frequency are both doubled, the reactance will be
s:
The capacitive reactance X is given by the formula:
X = 1 / (2πfC)

When both the frequency and capacitance are doubled (f' = 2f and C' = 2C):
X' = 1 / [2π(2f)(2C)]
X' = 1 / [4(2πfC)] = X / 4

Concept: Capacitive reactance represents the opposition offered by a capacitor to alternating current. It is inversely proportional to the product of frequency and capacitance (X ∝ 1/fC). Since both parameters are doubled, the denominator increases by a factor of 4, reducing the reactance to one-fourth of its initial value.

Options (A), (B), and (D) are incorrect because reactance decreases inversely rather than increasing or simply halving.

Correct Answer: (C) X/4
